title: The Biggest Migration on Earth Happens Every Night

scenes.text: Earth's biggest migration happens every night.
Trillions of sea animals rise from the deep as the sun sets.
Some climb from more than 3,000 feet down.
Lanternfish, krill, copepods, even octopus join the climb.
Scientists estimate about ten billion tons of animals move.
At sunrise, they all sink back down.

description:
Earth's biggest migration happens every night.
Every day, trillions of ocean animals rise toward the surface at dusk and sink back at dawn, an estimated ten billion tons of life on the move.
Did you know the ocean did this? Comment below.
first_comment: Which deep sea animal would you most want to see rise?
